deep.reconstruction:
The page has no mathematical derivation. It is a philosophical and programmatic draft for Riemann's natural-philosophy project, from the 1853 trial-lecture/Habilitation period. Its two parts are a set of excerpts on 'hypothesis' and the opening of the ether-gravitation hypothesis.

(A) Excerpts on 'hypothesis':
(i) Riemann's remark: Newton was far from the absurd idea that the explanation of phenomena could be obtained by abstraction.
(ii) Quotation from the General Scholium of Newton's Principia, ending 'Hypotheses non fingo'. The reading 'philosophiam experimentalem' is the 2nd-edition (1713) wording; the 3rd edition (1726) has 'naturalem'.
(iii) Arago, Oeuvres complètes, T.3, p.505, on Laplace's single venture into conjecture: the nebular cosmogony.
(iv) The Napoleon–Laplace anecdote: 'Sire, je n'avais pas besoin de cette hypothèse'.
These continue the previous page's point that 'hypothesis' now means everything added in thought to the phenomena, a broader sense than Newton's.

(B) Blatt 9, the physical programme.
- Newton's hypothesis, as Riemann reformulates it: at each time t and point x there is a determinate vector g(x,t). It is the resultant of all gravitational forces and gives every ponderable point there the same acceleration, independent of its mass. In modern terms this is a gravitational acceleration field g = -grad Phi with laplacian(Phi) = 4*pi*G*rho, and universality of free fall is the weak equivalence principle.
- Riemann's hypothesis: this cause is a state of motion of a substance (ether) that fills all of space continuously. Its motion is 'equal in magnitude and direction' to the force to be explained. The flow velocity u(x,t) is identified with g(x,t), or is proportional to it; the published version says the speed is proportional to the force.
- Consequence: every action of ponderable bodies on ponderable bodies across empty space is propagated by this medium. Hence light and radiant heat between celestial bodies must also be motions of the same substance.
- Gravitation and light propagation through empty space are the only phenomena that must be explained purely by motions of this substance.

The next page makes this formal. It writes the actual velocity as v = u + w, with u the gravitational part and w the light part, and takes the density to be constant (= 1), which implies div v = 0.

The following implicit consistency check is my addition. Outside masses div g = 0, since laplacian(1/r) = 0 for r != 0, so a velocity proportional to g is compatible with an incompressible medium in empty space. Inside matter div g = -4*pi*G*rho != 0. Riemann's published fragment accordingly lets ponderable bodies act as sinks of the ether.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page contains no computations.
Minor point: the identification 'motion equal to force' is dimensionally loose (velocity vs. acceleration). It must be read as proportionality, as the published version states.
The Newton quotation follows the 1713 2nd edition ('experimentalem'). It is accurate for that edition, though it differs from the 1726 text.

results.what: Gravity as a field: at each point a unique vector giving all bodies the same acceleration (universality of free fall).
Ether-flow model of gravitation: the velocity of a space-filling medium is proportional to the gravitational force; the same medium carries light and heat.
results.modern_name: Kinetic/ether (sink-flow) theory of gravity; unification of gravity and light in one medium
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's own fragment 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' (1853), published in his Werke (1876); related ideas from Euler, Challis, Bjerknes

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of material published in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke: the 1853 Naturphilosophie fragment and the philosophical fragments, including the Newton and Laplace quotations. It contains no new mathematics, only well-known programmatic statements and quotations.

checkable.asserts: Equals 0 for r != 0. The Newtonian potential is harmonic in empty space, so a flow proportional to g has zero divergence there, consistent with the constant ether density adopted on the next page.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,k=symbols('x y z k',real=True); r=sqrt(x**2+y**2+z**2); g=[-k*x/r**3,-k*y/r**3,-k*z/r**3]; simplify(diff(g[0],x)+diff(g[1],y)+diff(g[2],z))
checkable.asserts: Equals 0 away from the origin. A radial inflow with u proportional to g is a pure point sink, matching Riemann's picture of ponderable bodies absorbing the ether.
